extracted.intended_audience: readers of literary biography and those interested in 19th-century theatre/acting
extracted.subtask_description: Expository biographical material that also articulates principles and practical criteria for acting and stagecraft (selection of repertoire, delivery, physical embodiment, professional attitude, and mentorship). Useful for evaluating or training actors in dramatic art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult authoritative references for classical names/pronunciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice to consult Walker's Classical Pronouncing Dictionary when unsure of the names/pronunciations of classical/mythological figures (example: the boy was told, 'there is a book ... called Walker's Classical Pronouncing Dictionary, to which on all such occasions you can refer and find just what you want to know').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical production guidance: actors should use standard reference works to learn correct names/pronunciations; the anecdote emphasizes the value of self-education and of having reliable resources to consult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of dramatic art — selection and idealization
rubrics_metrics.description: "The true principle of the dramatic art ... [is] not merely to hold the mirror up to crude nature, but to give a choice and refined presentation of the truth. Nature ... is reality, but art is ideality. The actor is not to reflect all the direct and unrelieved facts of nature, but to present a selective and softened or intensified reflection of them. Art plays the tune of nature ... but with variations."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level aesthetic criterion for performance and production: acting should be a refined, selective presentation of reality rather than an unfiltered copy; performers should shape and idealize material to serve the art. (Text notes that Forrest personally disagreed with this view, illustrating competing schools.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Repertoire selection — favor higher tragedy over farce
rubrics_metrics.description: Holley urged Forrest to curb his taste for comic and farcical parts and as soon as possible to cease appearing in such characters, urging a deeper sense of his fitness for the highest walks of tragedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative/strategic guidance for career development: choose roles that cultivate and display higher tragic qualities when aiming for tragic eminence; avoid overindulgence in low comedy if pursuing serious dramatic stature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal qualities of an actor (sympathy, intelligence, observation, honesty)
rubrics_metrics.description: The text characterizes Edwin as 'sympathetic ... quick in intelligence, keen and eager in observation, and of an honest manner and make throughout,' and links these traits to dramatic genius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria for evaluating an actor's natural aptitude and temperament: empathy, sharp intellect, observational acuity, and an honest stage presence are flagged as foundational to strong performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acting technique — naturalistic emotional transitions and characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique praising Forrest: 'He assumes a stately majesty of demeanor, passes suddenly to wheedling hypocrisy, and then returns to the haughty strut of towering ambition, with a facility which sufficiently evidence[s] that he has ... well understood the immortal bard.' Also: 'In the soliloquies he uttered the sentiments as if they had arisen in his mind in that regular succession, and we never once caught his eye wandering towards the audience.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete performance criteria: fluid, convincing shifts between emotional states; physical embodiment of psychological turns; inner continuity that makes soliloquies feel spontaneously thought rather than recited; maintain focus (do not break eye contact or 'cheat' to the house).

rubrics_metrics.name: Soliloquy delivery — spontaneity and internal continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: "In the soliloquies he uttered the sentiments as if they had arisen in his mind in that regular succession" (i.e., soliloquies should read as interior thought rather than staged recitation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery guideline: arrange pace, emphasis, and breath so the speech appears to unfold naturally and logically from the character's mind; avoid gestures or looks that betray awareness of the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of intense physical realism to heighten effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Example of Forrest's tent scene: he 'sprang from his reclining posture, rushed forward to the foot-lights, and there fell upon his knees, with his whole frame trembling, his face blanched with terror, his sword grasped by the hilt in one hand and with the point in the floor, the sword itself so shaking that it could be heard all over the house.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stagecraft note: committed, sensory physical action and tangible bodily signs of emotion can make scenes sensationally effective; sound and visible physical detail increase audience impact. (Historical example of an innovative physical choice altering audience reaction.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic character embodiment including dialect and mannerisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim that Forrest 'was the first actor who ever represented on the stage the Southern plantation negro with all his peculiarities of dress, gait, accent, dialect, and manners.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for characterization: attention to socio-cultural dress, gait, accent, dialect, and manner enriches portrayal and can be historically notable; (note: this is a historical practice — modern ethical considerations regarding representation and caricature should be applied).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional attitude — treat applause as incentive, avoid complacency
rubrics_metrics.description: Moses Dawson's admonition: 'Applause should not be received as a reward, but as an incentive to still further exertion to deserve it.' Also caution against being 'intoxicated with success' and neglecting study and industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Career guidance: interpret praise as motivation to keep studying and improving; sustain discipline and continual learning rather than resting on laurels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek mentorship and continuous instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated references to the beneficial influence of experienced figures: a gentleman's advice about Walker's dictionary, Holley's interviews and instruction, the 'constant generous kindness and teaching of Mrs. Riddle' to Forrest, and conversations with Winfield Scott and John Howard Payne.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical professional standard: apprentice under and learn from experienced practitioners, accept critique and instruction, and cultivate mentors to accelerate development and correct defects.
